te: A 5-year work framework for the committee set (2024–2029)
se: The meeting considered the draft framework for the committee's work over 5 years (2024–2029), setting out its main roles: recommending policy, monitoring and evaluation, studying and analysing problems, promoting cooperation, and making recommendations to the government, so that security management is effective and can respond to changing threats
it: Draft work framework of the committee, 2024–2029

te: Preparations for bilateral meetings abroad, and a study visit approved (special meeting)
se: At a special meeting, the meeting considered preparations for a trip abroad for bilateral meetings to study military and security affairs, voted to select a main and a reserve service provider, assigned representatives of the committee to look into the details, and approved a study visit by the committee
it: Preparations for the committee's trip for bilateral meetings
Study visit by the committee

te: Working group set up to consider proposals on a national security structure
se: The meeting noted a draft proposal on the structure and framework of a study to develop Thailand's national security and military affairs, agreeing to set up a working group to consider the framework and details before bringing it back, and noted 2 Cabinet resolutions of 21 January 2025 relating to the committee, such as the draft law on defence civil servants' salaries
it: Draft proposal on the structure and framework of a study to develop national security and military affairs
Cabinet resolutions of 21 January 2025 relating to the committee

te: State agencies asked about their readiness in the event of war
se: Together with the Subcommittee on Holistic Security, the meeting asked about the readiness of government agencies should war make it impossible for people to live normally, including food, energy, communications and public order. Representatives of the Office of the National Security Council, ISOC and the agencies concerned explained their roles and contingency plans
it: Readiness of state agencies to provide basic necessities in the event of war

te: Complaint on boundary marker 73 and the highest point of Ko Kut received
se: The meeting considered a complaint in which the complainant alleges that boundary marker 73 and the highest peak on Ko Kut, which are reference points for Thailand's boundary through the median line, have been cited incorrectly, and invited the complainant to give information for its consideration
it: Complaint: boundary marker 73 and the highest point of Ko Kut, as markers that determine the boundary

te: The Directorate of Joint Intelligence heard, and 3 complaints received
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Directorate of Joint Intelligence, Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters, to report on the security situation and important military operations, and considered 3 matters referred to it: a request to examine the conduct of a doctor at a hospital, a petition for fair treatment from a former military officer, and a request to examine boundary marker 73 and the highest point of Ko Kut. It also set up a working group to prepare the annual work report
it: Security situation and military operations
3 complaints (a doctor's conduct · fair treatment for a former military officer · boundary marker 73, Ko Kut)
Working group set up to prepare the annual work report

te: Subcommittees' work followed up, and a study visit changed to a disaster relief training centre
se: The meeting followed up the progress of the subcommittees, approving the Subcommittee on Military Affairs' change of its trip on 17 January 2025 from the Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters to discussions and a study visit at the Disaster Relief Training Centre of the Armed Forces Development Command, Phanom Sarakham District, Chachoengsao Province, and noted the plan for a forum on research technology and new forms of threat
it: Change to the study visit of the Subcommittee on Military Affairs, to the Disaster Relief Training Centre, Chachoengsao Province
Plan for a forum on security research technology and new forms of threat

te: Subcommittee's working manual to be completed promptly
se: The meeting noted guidance from the Chair of the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security that all advisers should join working groups and that the subcommittee's working manual should be completed by mid-January 2026, so that each stage of work is clear and accountable, following on from the seminar presenting work plans
it: Guidance from the Chair of the committee on organising working groups
Preparation of the subcommittee's working manual

te: A work plan in 4 areas prepared for presentation at the committee's seminar
se: The meeting prepared to present its work plan at the committee's seminar "Review of Work in Fiscal Year 2025 and Preparation of the Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2026" (4 December 2025), with 4 issues approved in principle: research and development of unmanned aircraft, drones and counter-drone systems; military use of space; cyber security; and promoting the defence industry
it: Preparations to present the subcommittee's work plan at the committee's seminar

te: Working groups set up to study counter-drone systems and the military use of space
se: The meeting considered 2 work plan items for fiscal year 2026: approaches to promoting research and development of counter-drone systems, and a study of the use of the space domain in the operations of the armed forces. It resolved to set up working groups to study them and prepare reports, and will present the work plan to the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security
it: Approaches to promoting research and development of counter-drone systems
Study of the use of the space domain in the operations of the armed forces

te: Work plan for fiscal year 2026 set, with a focus on promoting the defence industry
se: At its first meeting, the subcommittee considered its work plan for fiscal year 2026, aiming for concrete work to promote the defence industry within its assigned duties and powers, and will present the outcome at the committee's seminar "Review of Work in Fiscal Year 2025 and Preparation of the Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2026" (4 December 2025)
it: The subcommittee's work plan for fiscal year 2026

te: The Department of Foreign Trade and the Customs Department give information on related laws
se: The meeting considered laws and regulations that may be obstacles to developing the defence industry, inviting representatives of the Department of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Commerce, and the Customs Department, Ministry of Finance, to give information and exchange views, in order to propose ways to remove limits on producing and developing military equipment in Thailand
it: Laws and regulations that may be obstacles to the defence industry

te: Review of the rules on procuring military equipment in crisis situations proposed
se: The meeting considered the armed forces' procurement of military equipment in crisis situations, observing that laws and regulations involve complex, lengthy approval steps that do not suit urgent needs, and proposed reviewing the laws and regulations on procuring military supplies in wartime to make them more flexible
it: The armed forces' procurement of military equipment in crisis situations

te: Prototype boots for minefield areas, and publicity for Thai-made firearms, discussed
se: The meeting discussed developing prototype boots for entering areas with landmines, observing that academic institutions or armed forces units should jointly develop and test them to reduce losses among personnel, and discussed publicising shooting competitions that use firearms made in Thailand
it: Development of prototype boots for minefield areas
Publicising shooting competitions that use firearms made in Thailand

te: Issues on the ISOC budget for 2026 prepared
se: The meeting considered issues on the expenditure budget of the Internal Security Operations Command (ISOC), for the committee's joint meeting with the ad hoc committee considering the draft Annual Appropriations Act for fiscal year 2026 on 31 July 2025, with observations on the budget for personnel development, most of which is for seconded posts, and on staff career progression
it: Issues on ISOC's expenditure budget for 2026

te: The Defence Industry Department gives information on laws that are obstacles
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Defence Industry Department to give information on laws that are obstacles to developing the defence industry, approaches to solving them, and progress. A private sector representative asked permission to attend and described the problems the private sector faces
it: Laws that are obstacles to developing the defence industry, and approaches to solving them
